title: Resolve lease-serialization glitch causing sticky inflight reservations and long-context tail
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Customer escalation: multiple customers (one Dedicated and two Private clusters) reported sustained extreme tail latency for short requests during mixed workloads. Investigations show persistent inflight reservations that never release for certain batches, causing backlog amplification and eviction thrashing on KV cache, which in turn starves short requests leading to long-context tail latency spikes. This ticket tracks the bug, mitigation, and long-term fix for a lease-serialization/handshake mismatch introduced during a private upgrade path (protobuf / versioning edge case).
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a Private runtime with mixed model variants (long-context and short-context) and enable continuous batching
Apply the upgrade that moved scheduler lease messages from v2->v3 protobuf schema without concurrent forward/backward compatibility guards
Run a synthetic workload: 70% short requests (<=128 tokens) interleaved with 30% long-context sessions (>=2048 tokens) distributed across tenants
Observe admission windows: short requests queue velocity drops while some inflight slots are held for >30s and never release
Capture scheduler logs and KV cache eviction traces to see repeated lease-id mismatches and failed prefetch handshakes
root_cause_analysis: During a rolling upgrade in Private clusters, the scheduler began emitting lease handshake messages using the v3 protobuf layout while some batchers and prefetch consumers remained on v2. The mismatch caused the prefetch handshake to acknowledge the lease locally but the serialized lease ID did not match the scheduler's expectation. As a result the scheduler never saw an explicit lease release for particular inflight reservations. Those reservations remained 'sticky' and blocked admission tokens and KV cache handoffs, causing eviction thrashing and backlog amplification. The issue is exacerbated under mixed-length workloads because long-context batches hold KV cache entries longer, further starving short requests.
mitigation: Hotfix: delay rollout of protobuf schema change and backfill compatibility shim in scheduler to accept both v2 and v3 lease encodings (patched and rolled out to affected dedicated/private clusters)
Emergency Canary: throttle admission for long-context priority class on affected hosts to restore short-request velocity
KV-cache heal: trigger controlled soft-evictions on hosts with sticky reservations to unblock cache handoffs
Customer communication: notify impacted accounts with steps taken and ETA for full fix
solution_plan: Implement robust lease-version negotiation: scheduler and batcher should exchange a version handshake and fall back to a canonical serialization when mismatch detected
Add deterministic lease TTL enforcement on the scheduler side (force-release stale leases after configurable grace window) with metrics and an admin override
Introduce a lease-reconciliation job that periodically scans inflight reservations and reconciles with worker state to detect and repair inconsistencies
Refactor prefetch handshake to be idempotent and tolerant to duplicate/renamed lease IDs, including adding a sequence number to detect reordered acknowledgements
Extend unit and integration tests to simulate cross-version rolling upgrades and mixed-length workloads to prevent regressions
rollout_plan: Ship compatibility shim (hotfix) to Private and Dedicated control planes first, monitor for 48 hours
If stable, roll the shim to Hosted runtime in a staged manner (canaries -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Deploy lease TTL enforcement as a guarded feature flag; enable on a small set of hosts and verify metrics
Deploy reconciliation job during maintenance windows with rate-limited repairs
Post-deployment: run a 72-hour observation window and keep admission throttle in place for long-context class until stable
qa_tests: Regression test: mixed-length workload harness with rolling upgrade simulation (v2->v3 handshake) validates no sticky reservations
Integration: simulate KV cache eviction pressure and ensure short-request latency SLOs remain within target under load
Chaos test: inject handshake serialization errors and confirm reconciliation job recovers within configured SLA
Performance: ensure lease TTL enforcement does not cause undue churn under healthy workloads
monitoring_and_telemetry: Dashboards: cross-tenant admission velocity, short-request 99th/99.9th token latency by host
Alerts: escalation when sticky_reservation_count > 5 on more than 3 hosts for 10 minutes
Logs: structured lease events with version and sequence_number for easier post-mortem
updates: 2026-03-08 - Ava: Created ticket after first customer support thread and initial triage. Reproduced locally in a Private dev cluster.
2026-03-09 - Ravi: Confirmed root cause is protobuf serialization mismatch across rolling upgrade. Drafted compatibility shim.
2026-03-10 - Lei (oncall infra): Deployed hotfix to affected Dedicated cluster; short-request velocity restored to baseline on that host.
2026-03-11 - QA: Integration harness shows reconciliation job can repair 98% of sticky reservations within 12s under test conditions.
2026-03-12 - PM (Lina Chen): Notified impacted customers, scheduled maintenance windows for Private clusters to deploy full fix. Estimate 5 story points assigned.
notes: This issue is distinct from eviction hysteresis and prefetch thrashing tickets; root cause is specifically serialization/version negotiation failure.
Avoid concurrent semantic schema upgrades without explicit two-way compatibility or negotiation handshake in future rolling upgrades.
Follow-on epic proposed: scheduler-versioned-protocols to formalize upgrade compatibility guarantees across runtime components.
